item.title: ANG increase Buka capacity
item.description: The National Flag Carrier Air Niugini, has increased its passenger and cargo capacity, on its flights to and from Buka, in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (AROB). Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer, Alan Milne in a statement says that this follows the opening of their new Jet A1 aviation fuel refueling facility, on the 30 th of September.
item.content:encoded:
The National Flag Carrier Air Niugini, has increased its passenger and cargo capacity, on its flights to and from Buka, in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (AROB).

Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer, Alan Milne in a statement says that this follows the opening of their new Jet A1 aviation fuel refueling facility, on the 30 th of September.

Mr. Milne says that the facility which is owned by Ok Tedi Energy, a subsidiary of Ok Tedi Mining Limited (OTML), will enable them to carry more passengers and cargo from Port Moresby to Buka and return, because they will now be able to refuel in Buka.

Mr. Milne also says that this is welcome news for the airline, because it improves aircraft efficiency, and it will further benefit communities and businesses, as they head into the festive period.

He also adds that a Fokker 100 was the first plane to refuel in Buka, when the facility was launched, and this saw them immediately clear a backlog of cargo from Port Moresby on that single flight.

Meanwhile, OTML Managing Director, Kedi Illimbit says, the project is part of Ok Tedi Energy’s push to strengthen PNG’s infrastructure, and provide fuel security and certainty.

item.title: Frieda River brings project information to West Sepik communities
item.description: Frieda River Limited has completed the first phase of its District Town Hall Engagements in West Sepik, taking information on the proposed Sepik Development Project directly to Local Level Governments and communities. The engagements covered Telefomin, Green River, Amanab, Vanimo town, Bewani and Maka Base in Walsa LLG, with government representatives also taking part.
item.content:encoded:
Frieda River Limited has completed the first phase of its District Town Hall Engagements in West Sepik, taking information on the proposed Sepik Development Project directly to Local Level Governments and communities.

The engagements covered Telefomin, Green River, Amanab, Vanimo town, Bewani and Maka Base in Walsa LLG, with government representatives also taking part.

The focus was to bring information about the project closer to the people and give communities an opportunity to hear from the project team, ask questions and understand where the development process currently stands.

For some elders, the discussions brought back memories of a project they first heard about when they were children, with the Frieda River Project having been under discussion in the Sepik region for more than 50 years.

FRL Country Manager Dr Joel Hamago said the long history of the project made direct engagement important, particularly for people who may not have had the opportunity to follow its development through formal processes.

He said the town halls were designed to allow communities to ask questions about the project's current stage, environmental requirements, proposed infrastructure and potential benefits and impacts.

The proposed Sepik Development Project includes the Frieda River copper-gold mine, hydroelectric power generation, a power transmission network, roads, pipelines, bridges, a proposed Green River Airport and Vanimo Ocean Port.

The project received six environmental permits from the Conservation and Environment Protection Authority in November 2025. The permits cover the proposed mine, hydroelectric project, power grid, infrastructure road, Green River Airport and Vanimo Ocean Port.

The project remains in the pre-development stage. Recent reporting has confirmed that construction is yet to begin and would proceed after the Special Mining Lease, or SML, is granted.

Dr Hamago told communities that FRL is now working through the requirements associated with the SML process and the next stages of project development.

Community questions during the town halls focused largely on employment, local business opportunities, landowner identification, benefit sharing and possible impacts on livelihoods and the environment.

Dr Hamago also explained the proposed Community Development Agreement, or CDA, including the distinction between direct and indirect benefits that could arise from the project.

He said a separate workshop would be organised for landowners and the wider public to provide more detailed information on the CDA process and how communities can participate.

The engagements were welcomed by communities, particularly the opportunity to receive information directly and ask questions about a project that could have long-term implications for the region.

The discussions also highlighted the importance of continued consultation as the project moves through its regulatory and development stages.

The second phase of the town hall program is expected to cover Aitape, Lumi, Yangkok and Nuku, extending the discussions to more communities across West Sepik.

The ongoing engagements will provide further opportunities for communities to understand the proposed project, while allowing project representatives to hear local concerns and expectations.

item.title: Coffee delays put farmers at risk
item.description: Coffee farmers in the Highlands could face further disruption to their income as the movement of coffee to Lae for export remains stalled during one of the busiest periods of the season. Coffee from producing areas, including as far as Mt Hagen, is transported by road to Lae, where it is prepared and transferred into shipping containers for international markets.
item.content:encoded:
Coffee farmers in the Highlands could face further disruption to their income as the movement of coffee to Lae for export remains stalled during one of the busiest periods of the season.

Coffee from producing areas, including as far as Mt Hagen, is transported by road to Lae, where it is prepared and transferred into shipping containers for international markets.

The stoppage is affecting the chain between growers and overseas buyers, with exporters holding coffee at warehouses and wharves while inspections and export clearances remain affected.

Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry president John Byrne said the disruption could have consequences well beyond the port, affecting growers, buyers, transport operators, storage facilities and workers who depend on the coffee trade.

“It’s not just the exporter that is affected. It goes right back to the grower,” Byrne said.

The situation is developing during the busiest month of the coffee export season, according to the LCCI. Exporters have reportedly slowed or stopped sending new coffee to Lae while the issue remains unresolved.

Coffee already packed in international shipping containers could also face additional costs if it has to be removed and transported back to the Highlands because of Lae’s humidity.

For farmers, delays in getting coffee from the Highlands to overseas markets could mean delays further along the payment and supply chain.

Byrne said the disruption also risks affecting Papua New Guinea’s reputation with international coffee buyers if orders cannot be fulfilled on time.

The export stoppage follows the transition from the former Coffee Industry Corporation to the National Coffee Authority, with administrative and financial authority issues affecting some operations, including export inspections and clearances.

LCCI is calling for the issue to be resolved quickly so coffee can continue moving from growers to international markets.

item.title: Three prisoner trucks strengthen police transport for Northern Command
item.description: Lae police will receive a new prisoner transport truck to help move prisoners between police cells, Buimo Correctional Institution and the courts. The truck is one of three new prisoner transport trucks handed over to the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary to support police operations across the Northern Command.
item.content:encoded:
Lae police will receive a new prisoner transport truck to help move prisoners between police cells, Buimo Correctional Institution and the courts.

The truck is one of three new prisoner transport trucks handed over to the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary to support police operations across the Northern Command.

Chief Inspector James Luan, Superintendent Operations with the Lae Metropolitan Command, said the new truck was urgently needed as the existing prisoner transport vehicle had developed mechanical problems.

“This is a timely presentation and a gift to us when we really need a good vehicle,” Luan said.

The truck will support both the Lae Metropolitan and Morobe Provincial commands in transporting prisoners to and from court.

Luan said the new truck would also support police operations during the 2027 National General Election.

“It will go a long way in the coming National General Elections as well,” he said.

The other two trucks will be used in Goroka and Madang.

Detective Sergeant Ben Payton of the PNG-Australia Policing Partnership said the three trucks were provided to the RPNGC at a cost of more than half a million kina.

“These trucks will be used in Lae, Goroka and Madang,” Payton said.

The new Hino trucks are fitted with prisoner cages, with separate areas for male and female prisoners. They are also equipped with lights and sirens.

Chief Superintendent Albert Beli, Provincial Police Commander for Eastern Highlands Province, said the truck allocated to Eastern Highlands would provide much-needed support for transporting prisoners.

“It’s a timely assistance given to us, especially to transport prisoners back and forth,” Beli said.

Superintendent Robert Baim, Madang Provincial Police Commander, said the new truck was a major relief at a time when police needed more resources to maintain manpower and operations.

“It’s a big relief, especially at this time that we are in dire need of resources to help us keep our manpower and our operations going,” Baim said.

The three trucks represent more than half a million kina in support of the RPNGC and are expected to strengthen prisoner transport and police operations across Morobe, Eastern Highlands and Madang.

item.title: Fariya Bridge cordoned off from public use
item.description: The Fariya Bridge near Dumpu Estate just before the Ramu Sugar Township, when travelling from the Madang side of the highway, is on the verge of collapse. Its current condition has forced the Department of Works and Highways to cordone off the bridge from public use.
item.content:encoded:
The Fariya Bridge near Dumpu Estate just before the Ramu Sugar Township, when travelling from the Madang side of the highway, is on the verge of collapse.

Its current condition has forced the Department of Works and Highways to cordone off the bridge from public use.

President of Usino Local Level Government, Charlie Wati told NBC News this morning that vehicles are currently using an access road inside the Oil Palm plantation.

Madang's Works Manager, Job Kull, has issued a road closure notice advising that the bridge is now closed to public use, and all motorists are told to use the company access road, which runs through part of the Oil Palm plantation.

Mr Kull explained that the bridge super structure (beam) has encountered severe damage (bending/ bulking) due to heavy loads and pressure exerted on it.

"It is therefore deemed unsafe for public use, and all vehicles are advised to use the company bypass for access to avoid accidents and further damage to other structures of the bridge, as well as allow proper investigation and eventual maintenance to restore accessibility," said Mr Kull.

Meanwhile, work on restoring the Numuru Bridge at Malala on Madang's north coast is underway.

The new bridge was brought in from Lae last weekend, and it's now on site.

According to Mr Kull, the new bridge at Numuru should be completed by the weekend, and ready for use.

item.title: NBC delivers weekend of live international sports
item.description: The National Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) has delivered one of the biggest weekends of live international sport in its history, bringing three marquee events across three time zones directly into the homes of Papua New Guineans. Over a single weekend, NBC broadcasted the Betfred Super League Grand Final from England, John Ume's bout in Auckland, New Zealand, and the London Broncos — all LIVE.
item.content:encoded:
The National Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) has delivered one of the biggest weekends of live international sport in its history, bringing three marquee events across three time zones directly into the homes of Papua New Guineans.

Over a single weekend, NBC broadcasted the Betfred Super League Grand Final from England, John Ume's bout in Auckland, New Zealand, and the London Broncos — all LIVE.

Managing Director of NBC, Kora Nou, said, for a nation that lives and breathes sport, it meant no waiting for highlights, no relying on secondhand updates, and no missing the moment.

“Last weekend was about one simple promise: if it matters to Papua New Guineans, NBC will bring it to them live.

“Our people watched our athletes and the world's best compete in real time, and they did it on their national broadcaster, for free.” He said.

Super League Grand Final: Old Trafford, live to PNG Rugby league is PNG's national game, and the Super League Grand Final is the pinnacle of the northern-hemisphere season.

NBC carried the decider between Wakefield Trinity and the Warrington Wolves on Saturday 3rd October live from Old Trafford, Manchester, with kick-off landing in the early hours of Sunday morning PNG time.

Thousands of fans stayed up across the country to watch Wakefield Trinity claim the 2026 title with a 23-10 victory.

The broadcast also gave Papua New Guineans the chance to follow our PNG heritage players, on the sport's biggest club stage in Europe. Delivering the Grand Final required NBC to receive and turn around a LIVE feed from the UK, a 10-hour time difference, and keep the signal stable through the night for viewers in every province.

John Ume in Auckland: a nation in his corner When John Ume stepped into the ring at Eventfinda Stadium in Auckland on Saturday 3rd October to face Hamza Perwaisy for the BX-9 Interim Welterweight Championship, the whole country was able to stand in his corner.

NBC broadcasted the fight live, so families, villages and workplaces could watch one of our own compete on an international card as it happened.

Ume delivered, stopping Perwaisy by technical knockout in the seventh round to claim the belt. It capped a strong run for Ume in the BX-9 series, where he has now won multiple bouts in Auckland.

The broadcast showed young Papua New Guineans what is possible when talent meets opportunity, and it put a PNG fighter in front of a home audience at the moment it counted.

For NBC, Auckland meant working with a separate rights holder and production team, a different feed path from the UK events, and a live window that had to be locked in alongside the rest of the weekend's schedule.

London Broncos: a Championship Grand Final rout, live Rounding out the weekend, NBC brought viewers the Betfred Championship Grand Final live, as the London Broncos crushed Doncaster RLFC 78-6.

The emphatic win gave PNG fans another window into English rugby league and a club with a growing following in the Pacific.

Carrying two UK grand finals in the same weekend proved NBC can run multiple international feeds back-to-back without dropping a beat.

Behind the screen: NBC's technical team Three live international events in one weekend was a genuine stress test, and NBC's engineers, technicians and production crew passed it.

The team managed incoming feeds from two countries, coordinated with multiple rights holders, and kept transmission running across overnight and daytime windows.

The weekend demonstrated capabilities that NBC has been building steadily:

“Our technical staff are the unsung heroes of last weekend,” said Mr Nou, “every live minute on screen was the result of hours of planning, testing and teamwork.

This is proof that NBC can deliver world-class live broadcasting.” Ready for a massive 2027 and beyond “Last weekend was more than a sports schedule.

It was a dress rehearsal for what lies ahead. “2027 will be one of the busiest years in NBC's history, with the 2027 National General Election, the Pacific Games, PNG's road to the NRL, and other regional and international events, including another two years of UK Super League (which NBC had already secured the broadcast rights for).

MD Nou said the experience gained last weekend will feed directly into NBC's planning for those events, including staff training, equipment investment and partnerships with international broadcasters.

NBC's goal is clear: to be the first and most trusted place Papua New Guineans turn to for live coverage of the moments that matter.

“We are building a national broadcaster that is ready for the big stage. What our team achieved this weekend gives us real confidence heading into 2027.

“PNG deserves to see its stories, its athletes and its nation live, and NBC will deliver,” Managing Director Nou said.

He also thanked the content partners, sponsors, staff and stakeholders for making the weekend's coverage ‘a resounding success.”

item.title: Police officers offered path to homeownership under housing scheme
item.description: Police officers across Papua New Guinea will now have the opportunity to buy and own their own homes under the newly established Police Home Ownership Scheme. ​A Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) was signed between the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary (RPNGC) and the National Housing Corporation (NHC), officially allocating 100 allotments at Duran Farm to RPNGC members.
item.content:encoded:
Police officers across Papua New Guinea will now have the opportunity to buy and own their own homes under the newly established Police Home Ownership Scheme.

​A Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) was signed between the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary (RPNGC) and the National Housing Corporation (NHC), officially allocating 100 allotments at Duran Farm to RPNGC members.

The Duran Farm allocation marks the first phase of a broader housing rollout.

NHC Managing Director Abel Tol confirmed that construction is already underway, with the first four-bedroom homes already built and work continuing on the remaining plots.

​Tol commended the RPNGC executive for establishing the housing scheme blueprint, which the NHC plans to replicate for other government agencies.

Police Commissioner David Manning highlighted that the scheme represents a strategic shift in police welfare—moving beyond basic barracks accommodation to ensure officers can retire with permanent homeownership.

​"This is an opportunity for our members to access housing ownership and mortgages, allowing them to build generational wealth by owning homes of their own," Commissioner Manning said.

​He added that securing long-term housing is essential for boosting frontline morale and supporting officers on duty.

Addressing officers in regional areas, NHC Board Chairman James Wong clarified that the government has directed the agency to identify 100 hectares of land nationwide to ensure provincial police officers are fully included in the scheme.

item.title: PNG commits K25 million to assist Tuvalu
item.description: Papua New Guinea has pledged K25 million over the next five years to support Tuvalu’s efforts to protect its coastline and reclaim land threatened by rising sea levels. Prime Minister James Marape announced this today at a joint press conference with Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Teo, shortly after arriving in Funafuti.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea has pledged K25 million over the next five years to support Tuvalu’s efforts to protect its coastline and reclaim land threatened by rising sea levels.

Prime Minister James Marape announced this today at a joint press conference with Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Teo, shortly after arriving in Funafuti.

Marape said Papua New Guinea would provide K5 million annually through its national budget to assist Tuvalu’s climate adaptation efforts.

The first payment of K5 million has already been transferred to Tuvalu’s Treasury to enable immediate work on coastal protection measures.

He announced this during the leaders’ segment of the pre-COP31 planning meetings, where Pacific leaders are discussing regional climate challenges ahead of the global climate summit.

Marape said the funding would be directed towards the Tuvalu Coastal Adaptation Project, a national initiative aimed at strengthening vulnerable coastlines and reclaiming safe land as the country grapples with the impacts of climate change and sea-level rise.

“This is an indication that whilst we wait for everybody else to respond, let’s do what we must do,” Marape said.

He also indicated Papua New Guinea’s readiness to provide additional assistance, including rock boulders and soil from its mountainous regions, should Tuvalu require physical materials for land reclamation projects.

Welcoming the contribution, Prime Minister Teo said the funding would play a significant role in protecting Tuvalu’s highly vulnerable coastline from ongoing erosion and sea-level rise.

“Declarations alone cannot physically fix eroding coastlines without substantial capital and resources,” he said.

While acknowledging recent international commitments on climate action, Teo noted that political declarations alone are insufficient to address the urgent challenges facing low-lying island nations.
